memory_update.text: Hammond Power Solutions should remain a priority underfollowed candidate for the dry-type transformer and power-quality node; verify official filings and US OTC investability before later-layer scoring.

Powell Industries is a high-relevance but less obscure electrical-distribution and switchgear candidate; later layers should test whether backlog quality is broad-based or driven by a small number of lumpy mega-projects.

Preformed Line Products is an adjacent transmission-hardware candidate, not a transformer pure play; keep it in the second-order lane and require stronger evidence linking order growth to grid buildout timing.

Need a dedicated follow-up search for US-listed micro/small-cap transformer, custom switchgear, power-quality, electrical magnetics, testing/inspection, and distributor names, including speculative exceptions below $300M only if exposure is unusually direct.

The chokepoint should be tracked as a cluster: dry-type transformers, medium-voltage switchgear, power-quality conditioning, substation components, and transmission hardware may all delay data center and industrial electrification projects before generation assets monetize.

HMDPF/HPS.A should be carried forward as the highest-purity direct node candidate for dry-type transformers, power-quality products, reactors, and electrical magnetics, with verification focused on data-center revenue materiality, backlog, pricing, capacity expansion, and lead times.

POWL should be carried forward as an adjacent underfollowed power-distribution equipment candidate, but its exposure must be decomposed by end market because legacy oil/gas and industrial activity may dilute the AI/grid-electrification thesis.

PLPC is not a direct transformer/power-quality play; treat it as a second-order grid hardware hypothesis tied to transmission and distribution buildout. Require evidence that Energy segment orders are accelerating from grid/data-center interconnection capex.

Need a dedicated follow-up search for U.S.-listed or OTC-listed niche manufacturers of reactors, harmonic filters, capacitor banks, voltage regulators, bus duct, power-quality monitoring, and transformer components; this pass found strong HPS/POWL/PLPC leads but may miss smaller component suppliers hidden inside broader industrial categories.

Add POWL as an underfollowed electrical-distribution candidate tied to medium-voltage switchgear, packaged power systems and behind-the-meter data-center power orders; key falsifier is lumpy mega-project concentration.
Add HMDPF/HPS.A as the most direct dry-type transformer and power-quality pure-play candidate; U.S. access is OTC, so liquidity and primary TSX listing must be tracked.

Add PLPC as a second-order grid/transmission hardware candidate adjacent to the transformer and power-distribution node; needs verification that AI/data-center grid capex is a real demand driver rather than narrative spillover.

The node should not be limited to transformer OEMs; include switchgear, packaged electrical buildings, power-quality filters/reactors, transmission hardware and specialized distributors when they can delay energization schedules.

Need a follow-up pass for distributors and certification/testing gates such as WESCO, Graybar-like private comparables, NETA testing contractors, transformer oil/material suppliers and electrical safety/certification labs.
HMDPF/HPS.A should be tracked as the cleanest discovered dry-type transformer and power-quality exposure, but it is US OTC rather than primary US exchange listed.

POWL maps strongly to medium-voltage switchgear, E-Houses, bus duct, and engineered power-distribution systems; evidence of large data-center orders moves it from generic industrial to direct power-chain candidate.
PLPC is not in transformers but is a second-order transmission/distribution hardware chokepoint candidate; survival in later layers requires order/backlog evidence linked to utility grid buildout.

The node should be broadened from dry-type transformers only to a schedule-critical electrical balance-of-system cluster: transformers, switchgear, E-Houses, bus systems, enclosures, PDUs, connectors, and T&D line hardware.

Need a focused later pass on distributors and channel bottlenecks such as WESCO-like electrical distribution, because transformer/switchgear shortages can be expressed through procurement and availability rather than manufacturing alone.
